title.en: Volume 407 Biographies 194: Jiang Zhongyuan Younger Brother: Zhong Ji, Zu Younger Brother: Zhong Xin, Luo Zenan
title.raw: 卷407 列傳一百九十四 江忠源弟：忠济 族弟：忠信 罗泽南

sentences.zh: 列傳一百九十四

translations.literal: Biographies 194
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 194

sentences.zh: 江忠源弟忠濟族弟忠信羅澤南

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan [younger brother Zhong Ji] [clansman younger brother Zhong Xin] Luo Zenan
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan; his younger brother Zhong Ji; his clansman Zhong Xin; and Luo Zenan

sentences.zh: 江忠源，字岷樵，湖南新寧人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan, style name Minqiao, was a native of Xinning in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan, styled Minqiao, came from Xinning in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十七年舉人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of the Daoguang reign he became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the seventeenth year of Daoguang (1837).

sentences.zh: 究心經世之學，伉爽尚義。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to statecraft; he was upright, forthright, and esteemed righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He steeped himself in practical statecraft and was known for his forthright, principled character.

sentences.zh: 公車入京，初謁曾國籓，國籓曰：「吾生平未見如此人，當立名天下，然終以節烈死。」

translations.literal: When he went to the capital on the metropolitan examination journey, he first called on Zeng Guofan. Guofan said: "In all my life I have never met such a man as this. He will make a name throughout the empire, yet in the end he will die a heroic martyr's death."
translations.idiomatic: On his journey to the capital for the metropolitan examination, he first paid a visit to Zeng Guofan, who told him, "In all my days I have never seen anyone like you. You will win fame across the realm—and yet you will die a martyr's death in the end."

sentences.zh: 大挑教職，回籍。

translations.literal: He was selected in the grand allocation for teaching posts and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned a teaching post in the grand allocation and went home.

sentences.zh: 察教匪亂將作，陰以兵法部勒鄉里子弟。

translations.literal: Perceiving that sectarian banditry would soon break out, he secretly drilled the local youths in his district according to military science.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that sectarian unrest was about to erupt, he quietly trained the young men of his district in military tactics.

sentences.zh: 既而黃背峒盜雷再浩果勾結廣西莠民為亂，一戰破其巢，擒再浩戮之。

translations.literal: Before long the brigand Lei Zaihao of Huangbei Cave did indeed collude with riffraff from Guangxi to raise a rebellion. In a single battle he broke their nest, captured Zaihao, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Huangbei Cave bandit Lei Zaihao did join forces with Guangxi ruffians to rebel. Jiang smashed their stronghold in one battle, seized Zaihao, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 以功擢知縣，揀發浙江。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to magistrate and assigned to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His service earned him promotion to magistrate and assignment to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 秀水災，奉檄往賑，遂權縣事。

translations.literal: When Xiushui suffered a disaster, he was ordered by dispatch to go and provide relief, and thereupon acted as magistrate in charge of the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiushui was stricken by famine, he was sent to administer relief and ended up acting as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 賑務畢舉，擒劇盜十數，邑大治。

translations.literal: When the relief work was fully accomplished, he captured more than ten notorious bandits, and the district was greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Once relief was complete, he rounded up more than a dozen major bandits, and the county was brought firmly under control.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吳文鎔待以國士，補麗水，檄治海塘。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Wu Wenrong treated him as a man of national stature, appointed him to Lishui, and dispatched him to oversee the sea dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wu Wenrong treated him as a premier talent, gave him the Lishui post, and put him in charge of the coastal dikes.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，曾國籓應詔薦其才，送部引見，尋以父憂去官。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended the throne, Zeng Guofan recommended his talent in response to an edict. He was sent to the ministry for audience, but soon resigned office on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Zeng Guofan recommended him by imperial edict. He was presented at court in the capital, then left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，大學士賽尚阿督師剿粵匪，調赴軍前，副都統烏蘭泰深倚重，事必諮而行。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign, Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took command to suppress the Guangdong rebels. Jiang was transferred to the front, and Vice Commander Ulan Tai relied on him deeply; on every matter he would consult Jiang before acting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851), Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a took field command against the Guangdong rebels. Jiang was called to the front, where Vice Commander Ulan Tai came to depend on him heavily and consulted him before every move.

sentences.zh: 忠源招舊所練鄉兵五百人，使弟忠濬率以往，號「楚勇」。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan recruited five hundred of the local militia he had formerly trained, had his younger brother Zhong Jun lead them thither, and they were styled the "Chu Braves."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan raised five hundred of the militiamen he had trained at home and sent his younger brother Zhong Jun to lead them. They were called the "Chu Braves."

sentences.zh: 賊氛方熾，官兵莫攖其鋒。

translations.literal: The rebel atmosphere was then at its height, and government troops did not dare meet their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel power was at its peak, and regular troops would not stand up to them.

sentences.zh: 忠源勇始至，偪賊而壘。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan's braves first arrived, they pressed close to the rebels and built fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Zhongyuan's men arrived, they pressed up against the rebels and threw up entrenchments.

sentences.zh: 賊輕其少，且新集，急犯之。

translations.literal: The rebels despised them as few in number and newly assembled, and pressed an attack on them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, judging them few and freshly gathered, attacked at once.

sentences.zh: 堅壁不出，逼近始馳突，斬級數百，一軍皆驚。

translations.literal: He held the walls fast and did not sally forth until they drew near, then charged out and beheaded several hundred; the whole army was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his walls and held his ground until the enemy came close, then burst out in a charge and took several hundred heads. The entire army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 累功賜花翎，擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was awarded the peacock feather, and promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated victories won him the peacock feather insignia and promotion to sub-prefect of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 賊聚永安，向榮與烏蘭泰不協，忠源調和，勿聽，知必敗，引疾回​​籍。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered at Yong'an. Xiang Rong and Ulan Tai were at odds; Zhongyuan tried to reconcile them but was not heeded. Knowing defeat was certain, he pleaded illness and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels massed at Yong'an, Xiang Rong and Ulan Tai fell out. Zhongyuan tried to mediate, but no one listened. Convinced disaster was coming, he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二年春，賊果突圍出犯桂林。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, the rebels did indeed break out of encirclement and attacked Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: That spring in the second year, the rebels broke out as he had foreseen and struck at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 忠源聞警，增募千人，偕劉長佑兼程赴援，未至，烏蘭泰傷歿於軍，自是獨領一軍，進扼桂林城外鸕鶿洲，三戰皆捷，圍尋解，擢知府。

translations.literal: Hearing the alarm, Zhongyuan raised another thousand men and, together with Liu Changyou, hurried to the rescue by forced marches. Before they arrived, Ulan Tai was wounded and died in the army. From then on Zhongyuan alone commanded a force, advanced to hold Luzhou outside Guilin, won three battles in succession, the siege was soon lifted, and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the news Zhongyuan recruited another thousand men and rushed to the rescue with Liu Changyou. Before they arrived, Ulan Tai was killed in action. Zhongyuan then took sole command, seized Luzhou outside Guilin, won three straight battles, broke the siege, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 賊竄全州，將趨湖南，忠源偕諸軍進擊。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Quanzhou and were about to press into Hunan; Zhongyuan advanced with the various armies to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped into Quanzhou and were heading for Hunan. Zhongyuan marched with the allied forces to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 賊陷城不守，復出竄，悉載輜重舟中，期水陸並下。

translations.literal: The rebels took the city but did not hold it, fled out again, loaded all their baggage into boats, and planned to advance by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the city but would not stay, broke out again, stowed all their supplies aboard boats, and planned a combined land-and-river advance.

sentences.zh: 忠源發樹塞河，截賊蓑衣渡，鏖戰兩晝夜，悍酋馮雲山中砲死。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan felled trees to block the river, cut off the rebels at Saoyi Ford, and fought fiercely for two days and nights; the fierce chieftain Feng Yunshan was killed by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan felled trees to dam the river and caught the rebels at Saoyi Ford. After two days and nights of bitter fighting, the rebel commander Feng Yunshan was killed by artillery.

sentences.zh: 賊棄舟夜遁，盡獲其輜重。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned their boats and fled by night; all their baggage was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned their boats and fled under cover of night, leaving all their supplies behind.

sentences.zh: 忠源先請扼東岸，未用其策，賊由東竄入湖南，陷道州。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan had first requested to hold the eastern bank, but his plan was not adopted; the rebels fled east into Hunan and took Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan had urged blocking the eastern bank, but his advice was ignored. The rebels broke east into Hunan and captured Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 又議賊眾不滿萬，慮日久裹脅眾，分防不如合剿，遠堵不如近攻。

translations.literal: He again argued that the rebel host did not number ten thousand, and that if the campaign dragged on they would press more people into service; divided defense was inferior to combined suppression, and blocking from afar was inferior to attacking close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: He argued again that the rebels numbered fewer than ten thousand and that, given time, they would swell their ranks by coercion. Concentrated assault was better than scattered defense, and pressing the attack was better than distant blocking.

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍合攻道州，賊堅壁，意在久踞。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various armies jointly attacked Daozhou; the rebels held their walls fast, intending to occupy it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies then besieged Daozhou. The rebels dug in, clearly planning a long occupation.

sentences.zh: 購城中內應，約期襲之。

translations.literal: He bought collaborators within the city and set a date for a surprise assault.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed agents inside the walls and arranged a coordinated strike.

sentences.zh: 賊走藍山、嘉禾，犯桂陽，陷郴州。

translations.literal: The rebels fled toward Lanshan and Jiahe, attacked Guiyang, and took Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated toward Lanshan and Jiahe, struck Guiyang, and captured Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 忠源謂後路進剿愈急，前路攻陷愈多，請仍申合剿之議，當事不省，賊益張，徑犯長沙。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan said that the more urgently the rear route was pursued in suppression, the more cities the forward route would see fall, and he again urged the plan of combined suppression, but those in charge did not understand; the rebels grew bolder and marched straight against Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan warned that the harder they pressed from behind, the more towns would fall ahead, and he renewed his plea for a united offensive. The authorities paid no heed. The rebels grew bolder still and marched straight on Changsha.

sentences.zh: 忠源偕總兵和春馳援，至則賊已踞城南，窟穴民廛，攻城甚急。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan hurried to the rescue together with the regional commander Hechun; when they arrived the rebels already held the south of the city, burrowed into the civilian lanes, and pressed the assault with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan rushed to the rescue with Regional Commander Hechun, only to find the rebels already holding the southern quarter, tunneling through civilian neighborhoods, and pressing the assault fiercely.

sentences.zh: 忠源望見天心閣地勢高，賊柵其上，驚曰：「賊據此，長沙危矣！」

translations.literal: Zhongyuan saw that Tianxin Pavilion stood on high ground with rebel stockades upon it, and exclaimed in alarm: "If the rebels hold this place, Changsha is in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan saw Tianxin Pavilion on its commanding height, with rebel barricades on top, and cried out in alarm, "If they hold that ground, Changsha is lost!"

sentences.zh: 率死士爭之，賊敗退。

translations.literal: He led dare-to-die troops to contest it, and the rebels were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He led a band of volunteers to seize it, and the rebels were driven back.

sentences.zh: 趣移壘逼賊，共汲一井，擊柝相聞。

translations.literal: He urgently shifted his encampment to press upon the rebels; they drew from the same well, and the night-watch clappers could be heard from one camp to the other.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his camp up against the rebel lines so close that both sides drew from the same well and could hear each other's night watches.

sentences.zh: 忠源弟忠濟自郴州尾賊至，約夾擊，為伏賊所傷。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's younger brother Zhong Ji, having trailed the rebels from Chenzhou, arranged a pincer attack but was wounded by ambushing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's brother Zhong Ji, who had pursued the rebels from Chenzhou, planned a pincer attack but was wounded in a rebel ambush.

sentences.zh: 縋入城商方略，因語眾曰：「官軍四面集，惟河西一路空虛。

translations.literal: He was let down into the city by rope to discuss strategy, and thereupon told the assembly: "Government troops are gathering on all four sides; only the route west of the river lies empty.
translations.idiomatic: He was lowered into the city by rope to confer on strategy and told the commanders, "Imperial forces are closing in from every side except the west bank of the river, which lies open.

sentences.zh: 賊奪民舟渡江掠食，食盡將他竄。

translations.literal: The rebels seize civilian boats to cross the river and plunder food; when provisions are exhausted they will flee elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are seizing civilian boats to cross the river for food. Once their supplies run out, they will break out somewhere else.

sentences.zh: 宜重兵扼迴龍塘。」

translations.literal: Heavy forces should be posted to hold Huilong Pond."
translations.idiomatic: We should mass troops at Huilong Pond to block them."

sentences.zh: 巡撫張亮基韙之，而諸將逡巡莫前。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Zhang Liangji approved this, but the various generals hesitated and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Liangji agreed, but the generals hung back and would not move.

sentences.zh: 時賽尚阿罷，徐廣縉代之，未至，城內外巡撫三，提督二，總兵十，莫相統攝。

translations.literal: At this time Sai Shang'a was dismissed and Xu Guangjin replaced him, but had not yet arrived. Inside and outside the city were three governors, two commanders-in-chief, and ten regional commanders, with no one to unify command.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shang'a had been removed and Xu Guangjin appointed in his place but had not yet arrived. Three governors, two commanders-in-chief, and ten regional commanders operated inside and outside the city with no one in overall command.

sentences.zh: 忠源赴湘潭，請於廣縉，不省。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan went to Xiangtan and petitioned Guangjin, but was not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan went to Xiangtan to plead his case to Guangjin, but again was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 賊卒由迴龍塘竄陷岳州，遂破武昌。

translations.literal: The rebels in the end fled through Huilong Pond, took Yuezhou, and thereupon captured Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels eventually broke out through Huilong Pond, seized Yuezhou, and went on to take Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 忠源痛謀不見用，不欲東。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan grieved that his plans were not employed and did not wish to go east.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter that his counsel had gone unheeded, Zhongyuan refused to march east.

sentences.zh: 張亮基奏留守湖南，剿平巴陵土匪，調赴瀏陽剿徵義堂會匪周國虞，斬馘七百，解散萬人。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji memorialized that he remain to guard Hunan, pacified the Baling bandits, was transferred to Liuyang to suppress the Zhengyitang secret-society rebel Zhou Guoyu, beheaded seven hundred, and disbanded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji had him kept in Hunan, where he pacified the Baling bandits, then sent him to Liuyang against the Zhengyitang rebel Zhou Guoyu. He killed seven hundred men and dispersed ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 瀏陽平，擢道員。

translations.literal: When Liuyang was pacified, he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Liuyang was pacified, he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，授湖北按察使，張亮基署總督，兵事悉倚之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he was appointed Hubei provincial judicial commissioner; Zhang Liangji acted as governor-general, and on all military affairs he relied entirely on Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he was made Hubei judicial commissioner. Zhang Liangji, acting as governor-general, relied on him for all military matters.

sentences.zh: 剿平通城、崇陽、嘉魚、蒲圻諸匪，擒其渠劉立簡、陳百斗、熊開宇等。

translations.literal: He suppressed the bandits of Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, Puqi, and other places, and captured their ringleaders Liu Lijian, Chen Baidou, Xiong Kaiyu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He put down banditry in Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, Puqi, and elsewhere, capturing ringleaders including Liu Lijian, Chen Baidou, and Xiong Kaiyu.

sentences.zh: 文宗知忠源忠勇可恃，命率所部赴向榮軍，尋命幫辦江南軍務。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor knew that Zhongyuan's loyalty and courage could be relied upon, ordered him to lead his command to Xiang Rong's army, and soon afterward ordered him to assist in managing Jiangnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong, knowing Zhongyuan's loyalty and valor could be trusted, ordered him to join Xiang Rong's army with his troops, then appointed him to assist in Jiangnan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上疏切論軍事，略曰：「粵寇之亂，用兵數年，糜餉二千萬，人無固志，地罕堅城。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he submitted a memorial sharply discussing military affairs, in summary saying: "The Guangdong rebel turmoil has employed troops for several years, consumed twenty million taels in provisions, men lack firm resolve, and places rarely have stout walls.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, he submitted a blunt memorial on military affairs that began: "The Guangdong rebellion has dragged on for years, devoured twenty million taels in supplies, left the troops without firm resolve, and offered few defensible cities.

sentences.zh: 臣出入鋒鏑，於今三年，謹策其大端，惟聖明裁察：一曰嚴軍法。

translations.literal: Your servant has gone in and out of spear-points and blades for three years to this day, and respectfully sets forth the main points for Your Sagely discernment: first, enforce military law strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has been in the thick of battle for three years now. I venture to set out the main points for Your Majesty's judgment. First: enforce military law rigorously.

sentences.zh: 將不行法，是謂無將；

translations.literal: If a general does not enforce the law, that is called having no general;
translations.idiomatic: A general who will not enforce the law is no general at all;

sentences.zh: 兵不用法，是為無兵。

translations.literal: if troops do not use the law, that is having no troops.
translations.idiomatic: and troops who will not obey the law are no army at all.

sentences.zh: 全州以失援陷而左次相仍，道州以棄城陷而潰逃踵接；

translations.literal: Quanzhou fell for lack of relief and retreats followed one upon another; Daozhou fell because the city was abandoned and routs and flight came in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou fell for want of reinforcements, and one retreat followed another. Daozhou fell because the city was abandoned, and rout piled upon rout.

sentences.zh: 岳州設防而不能為旦夕之守，九江列艦而不能遏水陸之衝。

translations.literal: Yuezhou set up defenses yet could not hold even overnight; Jiujiang arrayed warships yet could not check the land-and-water assault.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou was fortified yet could not hold for a single day. Jiujiang lined up warships yet could not stop the combined land-and-river advance.

sentences.zh: 豈有他哉？

translations.literal: Is there any other reason?
translations.idiomatic: Was there any other cause?

sentences.zh: 畏賊之念中之也。

translations.literal: The thought of fearing the rebels had taken hold within.
translations.idiomatic: Fear of the rebels had taken root in men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 賊嘗致死於我，而我不能致死於賊。

translations.literal: The rebels are always ready to die facing us, yet we cannot be ready to die facing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are always willing to die facing us, yet we are not willing to die facing them.

sentences.zh: 賊之戰也，驅新附於前，以故黨乘其後，卻則擊殺。

translations.literal: In the rebels' fighting, they drive the newly attached in front, have the old party press from behind, and if they retreat they are struck down and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In battle the rebels drive their newest recruits to the front, station veterans behind them, and kill any man who falls back.

sentences.zh: 故賊退必死而進乃生，我退必生而進則死，不待戰陣，而勝負分焉已。

translations.literal: Thus for rebels to retreat is certain death while to advance is to live; for us to retreat is to live while to advance is death—without waiting for the battle line, victory and defeat are already divided.
translations.idiomatic: For them, retreat means death and advance means life. For us, retreat means life and advance means death. Before the lines even meet, the outcome is already decided.

sentences.zh: 誠欲反怯為強，莫若易寬為猛。

translations.literal: If one truly wishes to turn cowardice into strength, nothing is better than changing leniency into severity.
translations.idiomatic: If we truly mean to turn fear into strength, we must replace leniency with severity.

sentences.zh: 皇上執法以馭將帥，將帥執法以馭偏裨，偏裨執法以馭兵士。

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty enforce the law to control generals; let generals enforce the law to control subordinate officers; let subordinate officers enforce the law to control soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty enforce the law upon your generals, let generals enforce it upon their officers, and let officers enforce it upon the rank and file.

sentences.zh: 避寇者誅，不援者誅，未令而退者誅。

translations.literal: Those who avoid the rebels shall be executed; those who do not reinforce shall be executed; those who withdraw without orders shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Execute any who shirk the enemy, any who fail to reinforce, any who retreat without orders.

sentences.zh: 法令既嚴，軍聲自壯。

translations.literal: Once the laws and orders are strict, the army's spirit will of itself grow strong.
translations.idiomatic: Once discipline is strict, the army's morale will stiffen of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 此討賊之大端也。

translations.literal: This is the great principle of suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first great principle of suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 一曰撤提鎮。

translations.literal: Second: dismiss the commanders-in-chief and regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Second: remove the senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 承平既久，宿將凋亡，提鎮大臣，積資可待。

translations.literal: Peace has lasted so long that veteran generals have withered away; commanders-in-chief and regional commanders rise by accumulated seniority and wait their turn.
translations.idiomatic: After so long a peace, the old generals are gone. Commanders-in-chief and regional commanders now advance by seniority alone, waiting their turn for promotion.

sentences.zh: 位尊則意為趨避，偏裨不敢與爭；

translations.literal: When rank is exalted their minds turn to evasion; subordinate officers do not dare contend with them;
translations.idiomatic: High rank breeds evasion, and junior officers dare not challenge them;

sentences.zh: 權重則法難驟加，督撫不能擅決。

translations.literal: when authority is heavy the law cannot quickly be applied, and governors cannot decide on their own.
translations.idiomatic: heavy authority makes swift punishment impossible, and governors cannot act on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 人情當齒壯官卑之日，輒思發奮為雄，位高則進取念衰，必不能踔厲以赴時會。

translations.literal: Human nature is such that when teeth are strong and office low, one always thinks to strive and become a hero; when rank is high the will to advance declines, and one certainly cannot leap forward to meet the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Men in their prime at the bottom of the ladder burn to distinguish themselves. Once they rise high, ambition fades, and they cannot throw themselves into the crisis at hand.

sentences.zh: 且軍興數載，饋餉滋艱，提鎮所需，較副參懸絕。

translations.literal: Moreover, with military campaigns running several years, provisions grow ever harder; what commanders-in-chief and regional commanders require differs from deputy and staff colonels by a vast margin.
translations.idiomatic: After years of war, supplies grow ever scarcer, yet what a commander-in-chief or regional commander costs dwarfs what a deputy or staff colonel requires.

sentences.zh: 裁一提鎮，養精兵二百而有餘。

translations.literal: Cut one commander-in-chief or regional commander, and there is surplus to maintain two hundred elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cut one such post and you could maintain two hundred crack troops with money to spare.

sentences.zh: 奚取以有限脂膏，奉此無益之提鎮？

translations.literal: Why take limited fat and grease to support these useless commanders-in-chief and regional commanders?
translations.idiomatic: Why pour our limited resources into these useless senior commands?

sentences.zh: 誠擇一深明將略者統制其間，餘則悉歸休致。

translations.literal: Truly choose one who deeply understands strategy to command among them, and let the rest all retire.
translations.idiomatic: Choose one man who truly understands strategy to command them, and send the rest into retirement.

sentences.zh: 副將以下，量擢其才。

translations.literal: From deputy commander downward, promote according to measured talent.
translations.idiomatic: Promote deputies and lower ranks strictly on merit.

sentences.zh: 此整軍之要道也。

translations.literal: This is the essential way to reorganize the army.
translations.idiomatic: This is the essential path to reorganizing the army.

sentences.zh: 一曰汰冗兵。

translations.literal: Third: eliminate redundant troops.
translations.idiomatic: Third: weed out useless troops.

sentences.zh: 選兵膽氣為上，堅樸次之，技藝又次之。

translations.literal: In selecting troops, courage comes first, stolid simplicity second, and skill third.
translations.idiomatic: In choosing troops, put courage first, stolid dependability second, and technical skill last.

sentences.zh: 質實耐苦之人，令進則進，令退則退，其身聽命於將而不知它。

translations.literal: Men of solid substance who endure hardship—ordered to advance they advance, ordered to retreat they retreat; their persons obey the general and know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Steady men who can endure hardship advance when told to advance and retreat when told to retreat. They obey their commander and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 浮怯之徒，無事則趨蹌觀美，臨陣則退縮旁徨，論功則鑽刺以圖美官，遇敗則推諉以逃咎戾，宜汰者一也。

translations.literal: Frivolous and timid fellows—when there is no affair they bustle and mince to look fine; facing battle they shrink and hesitate; discussing merit they bore in to seek fine offices; meeting defeat they shift blame to escape guilt—these should be eliminated, first category.
translations.idiomatic: The frivolous and timid strut in peacetime, hang back in battle, scheme for promotion when credit is handed out, and blame others when defeat comes. These are the first class to cut.

sentences.zh: 徵調頻煩，或羸老備籍，坐耗資糧，或部曲散亡，驚魂甫定。

translations.literal: With frequent levies, some are frail and old, kept on the rolls only to sit and consume provisions; some have units scattered and lost, their startled souls only just settled.
translations.idiomatic: Constant levies have left some men frail and elderly, kept on the rolls only to consume rations, and others with their units shattered, their nerves barely steady again.

sentences.zh: 當此餉糈匱絀，豈容更益虛糜，宜汰者二也。

translations.literal: At this time when rations and grain are exhausted, how can one allow further empty waste? These should be eliminated, second category.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies already exhausted, we cannot afford further waste. These are the second class to cut.

sentences.zh: 誠敕各營將領，討部曲而嚴察之，氣充膽壯者備攻剿，樸實堅苦者備屯防。

translations.literal: Truly command the officers of each camp to examine their units and inspect them strictly: those full of spirit and bold in courage are to be kept for attack and suppression; those plain, solid, and enduring hardship are to be kept for garrison and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Order every camp commander to inspect his unit rigorously. Keep the bold and spirited for offensive operations and the steady, hardy men for garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 捨此二端，盡歸釐汰，此致強之急務也。

translations.literal: Apart from these two categories, all are to be sifted out and eliminated; this is the urgent task for achieving strength.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone outside these two categories should be cut. This is the urgent work of building a strong force.

sentences.zh: 一曰明賞罰。

translations.literal: Fourth: clarify rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: make rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 勝有賞，敗有罰，亙古不變之常經也。

translations.literal: Victory has reward, defeat has punishment—an unchanging constant from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Reward victory and punish defeat: that has been the unchanging rule since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 顧勝有賞而賞非勝，則不如無賞；

translations.literal: Yet if there is reward for victory but the reward is not for victory, then it is better to have no reward;
translations.idiomatic: But if rewards are given for victory yet go to men who did not win, it would be better to give no rewards at all;

sentences.zh: 敗有罰而罰非敗，則不如無罰。

translations.literal: if there is punishment for defeat but the punishment is not for defeat, then it is better to have no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: and if punishments are imposed for defeat yet fall on men who did not lose, it would be better to impose no punishments at all.

sentences.zh: 無賞無罰，人猶冀賞罰之時；

translations.literal: With neither reward nor punishment, men still hope for the time of reward and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: With neither rewards nor punishments, men still hope that justice will come in time.

sentences.zh: 賞非其功，罰非其罪，則懲勸之用乖，怨讟之聲作，而軍事不可為矣。

translations.literal: when reward is not for merit and punishment is not for crime, then the use of chastisement and encouragement goes awry, voices of resentment and slander arise, and military affairs cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But when rewards miss the deserving and punishments miss the guilty, discipline collapses, resentment spreads, and the army cannot be led.

sentences.zh: 今戰勝有功，固當賞錄，左右侍從，獎敘尤多；

translations.literal: Now when there is victory in battle and merit, reward and record are certainly due, yet attendants at left and right receive commendation and promotion in especially great number;
translations.idiomatic: Today, when a battle is won, the victors ought to be rewarded—but court attendants receive the lion's share of commendations;

sentences.zh: 且未嘗行一失律之誅，按一縱寇之罪。

translations.literal: moreover, not once has the punishment for violating discipline been carried out, nor the crime of releasing rebels been prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: and not once has a man been executed for breaking discipline or punished for letting the enemy escape.

sentences.zh: 勝敗本兵家之常，主兵者每言勝而諱敗；

translations.literal: Victory and defeat are originally the constant of military families; those who command troops always speak of victory and conceal defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat are the common lot of armies, yet commanders speak only of victories and hide their defeats;

sentences.zh: 功過本無妨互見，主兵者輒匿過而言功。

translations.literal: merit and fault originally do not hinder appearing together, yet those who command troops always hide fault and speak of merit.
translations.idiomatic: merit and fault ought to stand side by side, yet commanders conceal their faults and trumpet their merits.

sentences.zh: 治承平天下且不可，況危亂之世哉？

translations.literal: To govern a peaceful realm under heaven is already impossible thus—how much less in an age of peril and disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct will not do even in peacetime—how much less in an age of crisis?

sentences.zh: 夫軍中賞罰未可一概論。

translations.literal: Now rewards and punishments in the army cannot be discussed in one uniform way.
translations.idiomatic: Military rewards and punishments cannot be applied by a single rule.

sentences.zh: 勝固當賞，或旅進取斬級以冒功，或追擊貪貨財而得小，則當罰；

translations.literal: Victory certainly should be rewarded, yet if a company advances to take heads and claim merit falsely, or in pursuit greedily seizes goods and gains only small results, then they should be punished;
translations.idiomatic: Victory deserves reward, yet if men advance in a mob merely to claim heads and steal credit, or break off pursuit to plunder and win only a trifling gain, they deserve punishment;

sentences.zh: 敗固當罰，或邁勇先驅，後援不繼，或大軍已卻，一將獨前，則當賞。

translations.literal: Defeat certainly should be punished, yet if one strides forward bravely as vanguard but rear support does not follow, or the great army has already withdrawn while one general advances alone, then he should be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat deserves punishment, yet if a man charges ahead as vanguard while reinforcements fail to follow, or the army retreats while one officer presses forward alone, he deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 今大帥據營將之言，營將恃左右之口。

translations.literal: Now the supreme commander relies on what camp generals say, and camp generals rely on the mouths of those at their side.
translations.idiomatic: Today the commander-in-chief trusts only what his camp generals tell him, and they in turn trust only their aides.

sentences.zh: 功罪之實，非採訪所可知，好惡之心，因毀譽而多舛。

translations.literal: The reality of merit and fault cannot be known through inquiry; hearts of liking and disliking, swayed by praise and blame, are often wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The truth of who deserves credit or blame cannot be learned by hearsay, and personal favor and dislike, shaped by gossip, are often mistaken.

sentences.zh: 求是非洽乎人心，難矣。

translations.literal: To seek right and wrong in accord with men's hearts is difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To judge right and wrong in a way the troops will accept is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 自非親歷行陣，開誠佈公，何以慰軍士之心而振披靡之習？

translations.literal: Unless one personally experiences the battle line and opens one's heart with public fairness, how can one comfort soldiers' hearts and revive the habit of rout?
translations.idiomatic: Unless the commander goes to the front himself and deals openly and fairly, how can he steady the troops' hearts and break the habit of panic flight?

sentences.zh: 此風氣不可不急為振拔者也。

translations.literal: This atmosphere cannot but be urgently revived and lifted up.
translations.idiomatic: This corruption of morale must be reversed without delay.

sentences.zh: 一曰戒浪戰。

translations.literal: Fifth: guard against reckless fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: avoid reckless battles.

sentences.zh: 用兵之道，能守而後能戰，能制人而後不制於人，能避賊之長而後可用吾之短。

translations.literal: The way of employing troops: one must be able to defend before one can fight, able to control others before one is not controlled by others, able to avoid the rebels' strengths before one can use our weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: The art of war demands that one defend before one attacks, control the enemy before being controlled, and avoid the rebels' strengths before exploiting our own advantages.

sentences.zh: 臣自廣西以來，深觀賊勢，結營則因地築壘，環以深壕；

translations.literal: Your servant, since Guangxi, has closely observed rebel strength: when they make camp they build ramparts according to the terrain and ring them with deep moats;
translations.idiomatic: Since Guangxi I have studied the rebels closely. When they camp, they build earthworks suited to the ground and ring them with deep trenches;

sentences.zh: 置陣則正兵敵前，奇兵旁襲；

translations.literal: when they deploy formations the regular troops face the enemy while surprise troops strike from the flank;
translations.idiomatic: in battle they put regular troops in front and strike from the flanks with ambush forces;

sentences.zh: 止則遍購徒黨，伺吾虛實；

translations.literal: when halted they buy followers everywhere and spy on our strength and weakness;
translations.idiomatic: when they halt they recruit agents everywhere to watch our movements;

sentences.zh: 行則遙壯聲威，乘吾張皇。

translations.literal: when marching they magnify their fame from afar and take advantage of our panic.
translations.idiomatic: when they march they inflate their reputation from afar and strike when we are in disarray.

sentences.zh: 故嘗以為賊止則當扼要以斷其饋濟，嚴兵以截其奔逃；

translations.literal: Thus I have always held that when rebels halt one should hold strategic points to cut off their supplies, and post strict troops to intercept their flight;
translations.idiomatic: I have long held that when the rebels stop, we should seize key points to cut their supplies and post strong forces to block their escape;

sentences.zh: 賊行則當逆擊以遏其鋒，設伏以撓其勢。

translations.literal: when rebels march one should strike against them to check their edge and set ambushes to thwart their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: when they march we should meet them head-on to blunt their advance and lay ambushes to break their momentum.

sentences.zh: 乃我之圍賊不嚴守而攻堅，追賊不截歸而尾擊，小有挫失，士氣先頹。

translations.literal: Yet in our encirclement of rebels we do not hold strictly but assault stout walls; in pursuit we do not cut off retreat but tail-strike; with a small setback morale first collapses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we besiege without holding our lines and assault walled cities head-on; we pursue without cutting off retreat and merely chase from behind. At the slightest setback morale collapses.

sentences.zh: 此兵法不可不變計者也。

translations.literal: On this point military method cannot but change its plans.
translations.idiomatic: Our tactics must change.

sentences.zh: 一曰察地勢。

translations.literal: Sixth: observe terrain and position.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: read the terrain.

sentences.zh: 勢者非圖史所載山川一定之險也。

translations.literal: Position is not the fixed peril of mountains and rivers recorded in maps and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Strategic advantage is not the fixed terrain marked on maps and histories.

sentences.zh: 視賊出入之途，先為之防，察賊分合之機，遙為之制；

translations.literal: Watch the rebels' routes in and out and defend against them beforehand; observe the rebels' moments of dividing and combining and control them from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Watch where the rebels come and go and block them in advance; observe when they split or unite and control them from a distance;

sentences.zh: 則漸車之澮，數仞之岡，苟形勢在所必爭，即事機不容或失。

translations.literal: then a ford where a cart can barely cross, a mound several ren high—if the configuration must be contested, the opportunity cannot be allowed to slip.
translations.idiomatic: then even a shallow ford or a low hill, if the ground must be fought for, must not be lost for an instant.

sentences.zh: 全州蓑衣渡之戰，寇焰已摧，宜速壁河東斷其右臂；

translations.literal: At the battle of Saoyi Ford in Quanzhou the rebel flame was already broken; one should quickly wall the east bank of the river and cut off their right arm;
translations.idiomatic: After the battle at Saoyi Ford in Quanzhou had broken the rebels' momentum, we should have fortified the east bank at once and severed their line of retreat;

sentences.zh: 道州之役，寇鋒已挫，宜分屯七里橋扼其東趨；

translations.literal: in the Daozhou campaign the rebel edge was already blunted; one should have divided forces to garrison Qili Bridge and choke their eastward thrust;
translations.idiomatic: after Daozhou had blunted their advance, we should have posted troops at Qili Bridge to block their eastward march;

sentences.zh: 長沙將解圍，則宜堅壁迴龍潭、土橋頭，使賊不得西犯。

translations.literal: when Changsha was about to be relieved from siege, one should have held walls fast at Huilong Pond and Tuqiaotou so the rebels could not violate the west.
translations.idiomatic: as Changsha was about to be relieved, we should have fortified Huilong Pond and Tuqiaotou so the rebels could not break westward.

sentences.zh: 它若道州蓮花池、蓮濤灣，死地六十里，而縱之使生；

translations.literal: Elsewhere, at Daozhou's Lotus Pond and Liantao Bay—sixty li of dead ground—yet they were let go and given life;
translations.idiomatic: At Daozhou's Lotus Pond and Liantao Bay—a sixty-li killing ground—we let them escape alive;

sentences.zh: 湘陰臨資口、岳州城陵磯皆必爭之區，而縱之使遁。

translations.literal: Xiangyin's Linzikou and Yuezhou's Chenglingji are all ground that must be contested, yet they were let go and allowed to slip away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyin's Linzikou and Yuezhou's Chenglingji were ground we had to hold, yet we let the enemy slip through.

sentences.zh: 禍機在咫尺之間，流毒遂在千里之外。

translations.literal: The seed of calamity lay within a foot's reach, and the spreading poison then extended a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster was sown within arm's reach, and its poison spread a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 此敗轍之不可不深鑑者也。

translations.literal: These tracks of defeat cannot but be deeply taken as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: These defeats must be studied as a stern warning.

sentences.zh: 一曰嚴約束。

translations.literal: Seventh: enforce strict discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: enforce strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 殺賊所以安民，安民乃可殺賊。

translations.literal: Killing rebels is how one secures the people; only when the people are secured can one kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: We kill rebels to secure the people, and only by securing the people can we kill rebels.

sentences.zh: 粵寇慘虐，不可勝言，然擇肥而噬，窮簷不暇搜求。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebels' cruelty is beyond words, yet they choose the fat to devour and have no leisure to search out poor eaves.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong rebels' cruelty beggars description, yet they prey on the wealthy and rarely bother the poorest households.

sentences.zh: 或偽結民心，多償市直。

translations.literal: Sometimes they falsely win popular hearts and pay generously at market prices.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they feign goodwill and pay fair prices in the markets.

sentences.zh: 兵則攫取姦污，窮戶且難倖免。

translations.literal: Troops seize and violate; even poor households can hardly escape.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops seize goods and commit outrages from which even the poorest households cannot escape.

sentences.zh: 故於賊且有恕詞，於兵能無怨毒。

translations.literal: Thus toward rebels there are even words of forgiveness, while toward troops how can there be no bitter resentment?
translations.idiomatic: The people may even make excuses for the rebels, yet how can they feel anything but hatred toward our soldiers?

sentences.zh: 且長夫估客，遊蕩無常，託偽營裝，恣行淫掠，鄉民畏懼，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Moreover, porters and merchants wander without fixed abode, falsely claim camp garb, and wantonly commit rape and plunder; villagers fear them and dare not call them to account.
translations.idiomatic: Porters and merchants drift without fixed posts, pose as soldiers, and loot and assault at will. Villagers are terrified and dare not resist.

sentences.zh: 應敕諸營首嚴防制，備冊時稽。

translations.literal: Each camp head should be commanded to enforce strict control, keep registers, and inspect on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Every camp commander should be ordered to enforce strict control, keep registers, and inspect them regularly.

sentences.zh: 犯則軍法按行，絕其芽蘗。

translations.literal: Offenders shall be dealt with by military law and their sprouts cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Violators should be punished under military law before the evil spreads.

sentences.zh: 此結民心毖後患之要圖也。

translations.literal: This is the essential plan for winning popular hearts and preventing later troubles.
translations.idiomatic: This is essential to winning the people's loyalty and preventing future trouble.

sentences.zh: 一曰寬脅從。

translations.literal: Eighth: show leniency to the coerced.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: show leniency to those coerced into service.

sentences.zh: 粵寇徒黨，喪亡實多，煨燼之餘，類多附脅。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebel followers have in truth suffered many deaths; among the embers and ashes, most are attached under coercion.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel ranks have suffered heavy losses; what remains are mostly men pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 平昔會徒盜賊，寬典相蒙，監禁軍流，乘時放逸，命為前導，尤所甘心。

translations.literal: Former secret-society members and bandits, shielded by lenient statutes, imprisoned or banished to the army, released when the time came, appointed as vanguards—they are especially willing.
translations.idiomatic: Former secret-society men and bandits, shielded by lenient laws, or convicts and exiles released in the crisis and sent as guides, serve the rebels willingly.

sentences.zh: 凡此法無可逭，自爾獲焉必殺。

translations.literal: All such as these have no escape under the law; once captured they must be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Such men have no excuse under the law and must be executed once captured.

sentences.zh: 至若良民驅迫，骨肉羈縻，此中進退維谷之忱，艱苦顛連之狀，每一念及，輒用隱傷。

translations.literal: As for good commoners driven under compulsion, kin bound and tethered—the anguish of advance and retreat in a dilemma, the hardship of repeated overturnings—each time I think of it I am secretly wounded.
translations.idiomatic: But good people driven under duress, families torn apart—the anguish of men trapped between two fires, the misery of lives overturned again and again—fills me with private grief whenever I think of it.

sentences.zh: 宜敕各營刊示射達，臨陣建免死之旗，令其倒戈以赴，曲賜保全。

translations.literal: Each camp should be commanded to post notices and shoot them forth to reach all; on the battlefield raise a banner granting exemption from death, order them to turn their blades and come over, and bend to grant them preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Every camp should post proclamations far and wide, raise a banner on the battlefield promising immunity from death, and invite coerced men to turn their weapons and come over in safety.

sentences.zh: 既可探賊情，復以攜賊黨。

translations.literal: This both can probe rebel intelligence and again can win over rebel factions.
translations.idiomatic: This will both yield intelligence and peel away the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 此尤好生盛德，討賊機宜之大權也。

translations.literal: This is especially the great virtue of cherishing life and the great authority of opportune measures for suppressing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: This is both an act of humane governance and a powerful tactic for defeating the rebels.

sentences.zh: 行此八者，破格以攬奇才，便宜以畀賢帥，擇良吏以固根本，嚴綜覈以裕餉源。

translations.literal: If these eight are carried out, break rules to gather extraordinary talent, grant discretionary authority to worthy commanders, choose good officials to solidify the foundation, and enforce strict comprehensive audit to enrich the source of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: If these eight measures are adopted—recruit exceptional talent without regard to convention, give able commanders full discretion, appoint good officials to secure the foundations, and audit supplies rigorously to keep the army fed—

sentences.zh: 如此而盜賊不滅，盛治不興，原斬臣首以謝天下。」

translations.literal: if bandits and rebels are still not extinguished and flourishing governance still does not arise, your servant begs that his head be cut off to answer to all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: and yet the rebels are not destroyed and good order does not return, I beg that my head be struck off to answer to the empire."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne, and the Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 行至九江，聞南昌被圍，方有旨促援鳳陽，疏請先援江西，率兵千三百人，三晝夜馳抵南昌。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiujiang he heard Nanchang was besieged; an edict had just urged relief for Fengyang, but he memorialized requesting first to relieve Jiangxi, led thirteen hundred troops, and in three days and nights galloped to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang he learned that Nanchang was under siege. Though an edict had just ordered him to relieve Fengyang, he memorialized to rescue Jiangxi first, led thirteen hundred men, and reached Nanchang after three days and nights of forced marches.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張芾舉王命旗牌授忠源，戰守事悉聽指揮。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Zhang Fu raised the imperial mandate banner and tablet and gave them to Zhongyuan; all matters of fighting and defending were entirely subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Fu presented him with the imperial mandate banner and gave him full command of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 忠源火城外廛廬，斬逃者，謂章江門最受敵，自當之，日登城督戰。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan burned the shops and dwellings outside the city, beheaded deserters, said Zhangjiang Gate bore the heaviest attack and took that post himself, and daily climbed the wall to supervise battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan burned the buildings outside the walls and executed deserters. Saying Zhangjiang Gate faced the heaviest assault, he took that sector himself and went up on the walls every day to direct the fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊穴地轟城，崩數十丈。

translations.literal: The rebels tunneled underground and blasted the wall, collapsing several tens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tunneled under the wall and blew a breach dozens of feet wide.

sentences.zh: 刃斃先登賊，囊土填缺。

translations.literal: He killed with the blade the rebels who first climbed up, and filled the gap with bags of earth.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the rebels who had broken through and had the breach filled with sandbags.

sentences.zh: 數突門出戰，夜遣死士縋下焚賊營。

translations.literal: Several times he burst from the gates to fight; at night he sent dare-to-die men lowered by rope to burn the rebel camps.
translations.idiomatic: He led several sorties through the gates and at night lowered volunteers by rope to burn the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉獎，被珍賚。

translations.literal: An edict praised and rewarded him, and he received precious gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and bestowed precious gifts.

sentences.zh: 尋湖南援師至，分軍扼樟樹鎮，遣羅澤南剿平泰和、萬安、安福土匪。

translations.literal: Soon Hunan relief troops arrived; he divided forces to hold Zhangshu Town and dispatched Luo Zenan to suppress and pacify the bandits of Taihe, Wan'an, and Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan reinforcements soon arrived. He posted troops at Zhangshu Town and sent Luo Zenan to pacify banditry in Taihe, Wan'an, and Anfu.

sentences.zh: 守南昌九十餘日，至八月，屢砲毀賊壘，沉賊船，乘風縱火，賊乃遁。

translations.literal: He defended Nanchang for more than ninety days; by the eighth month he repeatedly destroyed rebel stockades with cannon, sank rebel boats, and set fires with the wind; the rebels then fled.
translations.idiomatic: After defending Nanchang for more than ninety days, by the eighth month repeated artillery fire had smashed rebel fortifications and sunk their boats. When he set fires with the wind at his back, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其功，加二品頂戴。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit and added the second-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his achievement and granted him the second-rank official insignia.

sentences.zh: 賊退據九江，分擾湖北興國，迳犯田家鎮。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew to hold Jiujiang, divided forces to harass Xingguo in Hubei, and marched straight to attack Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back on Jiujiang, raided Xingguo in Hubei, and marched straight on Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 忠源赴援，部兵二千，途阻不能遽達，先挈親兵數十人抵田家鎮。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan went to the rescue with two thousand troops under his command; the route was blocked and he could not arrive quickly, so he first took several tens of personal guards and reached Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan hurried to the rescue with two thousand men but was delayed on the road. He pushed ahead with a few dozen personal guards and reached Tianjiazhen first.

sentences.zh: 甫一日，賊舟乘風大至，道員徐豐玉等死之。

translations.literal: After only one day rebel boats came in great force with the wind; Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu and others died.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day rebel boats swept in on a favorable wind. Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 忠源自劾，詔原之，降四級留任，尋擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan impeached himself; an edict pardoned him, reduced him four grades but retained him in office, and soon afterward promoted him to Anhui provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan submitted a self-accusation. The court pardoned him, demoted him four ranks while keeping him in post, and soon afterward appointed him governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 賊已陷黃州、漢陽，圍武昌。

translations.literal: The rebels had already taken Huangzhou and Hanyang and were besieging Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already taken Huangzhou and Hanyang and were besieging Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 沿江擊賊，敗之，武昌解嚴。

translations.literal: He struck the rebels along the river, defeated them, and Wuchang was relieved from martial law.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the rebels along the river, defeated them, and lifted the siege of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 疏請增兵萬人，當淮南一路，而湖北留其兵不盡遣，僅率兵二千冒雨行。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting ten thousand additional troops to hold the Huainan route, but Hubei retained his troops and did not send them all; he led only two thousand men marching in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for ten thousand more troops to hold the Huainan front, but Hubei held back most of his force. He marched on with only two thousand men in the rain.

sentences.zh: 將士疲頓，忠源亦遘疾。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were exhausted; Zhongyuan also fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were exhausted, and Zhongyuan himself fell ill.

sentences.zh: 至六安，賊已陷桐城、舒城。

translations.literal: When he reached Lu'an, the rebels had already taken Tongcheng and Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Lu'an, the rebels had already captured Tongcheng and Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 吏民遮留，不可，留千人守六安，舁疾抵廬州。

translations.literal: Officials and people blocked him to detain him, but he could not stay; he left a thousand men to guard Lu'an and was carried in his illness to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and townspeople begged him to stay, but he could not. He left a thousand men at Lu'an and was carried, ill, to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 部署未定，賊已大至。

translations.literal: Before deployment was settled, the rebels had arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Before his dispositions were complete, the rebels were upon him in force.

sentences.zh: 城中合援兵團勇僅三千人，忠源力疾守陴，迭挫撲城之賊。

translations.literal: Within the city, relief troops and militia together numbered only three thousand; Zhongyuan, forcing himself despite illness, defended the parapets and repeatedly repulsed rebels storming the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops and militia inside the city numbered only three thousand. Though gravely ill, Zhongyuan held the walls and repeatedly beat back assaults.

sentences.zh: 地道轟城屢圮，皆奮擊卻之。

translations.literal: Underground tunnels blasted the wall and it collapsed repeatedly; each time he fought fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel mines repeatedly blew gaps in the walls, and each time he fought them off.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉忠源力保危城，躬馳戰陣，賜號霍隆武巴圖魯。

translations.literal: An edict praised Zhongyuan for strenuously preserving the perilous city and personally charging the battle line, and granted him the title Huolongwu Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Zhongyuan for holding the endangered city and fighting at the front in person, and granted him the title Huolongwu Batulu.

sentences.zh: 時陝甘總督舒興阿兵萬餘，畏葸不進。

translations.literal: At this time Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Shu Xing'a had more than ten thousand troops but, fearful and hesitant, would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shu Xing'a of Shaanxi-Gansu had more than ten thousand men nearby but hung back in fear and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 忠源弟忠濬偕劉長佑來援，駐城外五里墩，阻不得前。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's younger brother Zhong Jun came to the rescue together with Liu Changyou, encamped at Wulidun outside the city, but was blocked and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's brother Zhong Jun came with Liu Changyou to relieve the city and camped at Wulidun outside the walls, but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 被圍月餘，廬州知府胡元煒陰通賊，賊知城中食乏，軍火將盡，攻益急。

translations.literal: Besieged for more than a month, Luzhou Prefect Hu Yuanwei secretly communicated with the rebels; the rebels knew provisions in the city were scarce and munitions nearly exhausted, and pressed the attack ever more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month under siege, Luzhou Prefect Hu Yuanwei was secretly in league with the rebels. Learning that food was short and ammunition nearly gone, they redoubled their assault.

sentences.zh: 水西門圮，且戰且修築。

translations.literal: The West Water Gate collapsed; he fought even as he repaired and built.
translations.idiomatic: The West Water Gate collapsed. He fought even as his men rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 賊突自南門緣梯入，忠源掣刀自刎。

translations.literal: Rebels burst in from the South Gate climbing ladders; Zhongyuan drew his blade to cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels broke in through the South Gate on scaling ladders. Zhongyuan drew his sword to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 左右持之，一僕負之行，忠源奮脫。

translations.literal: Those at his side held him; one servant carried him as he walked, but Zhongyuan struggled free.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants seized him. A servant tried to carry him away, but Zhongyuan broke free.

sentences.zh: 轉戰至水閘橋，身受七創，投古塘死之。

translations.literal: Fighting his way to Shuizha Bridge, he received seven wounds, threw himself into Gutang Pond, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way to Shuizha Bridge, took seven wounds, and threw himself into Gutang Pond to die.

sentences.zh: 布政使劉裕珍，池州知府陳源兗，同知鄒漢勳、鬍子雝，縣丞興福、艾延輝，副將鬆安，參將馬良、戴文淵，同時殉難。

translations.literal: Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Yuzhen, Chizhou Prefect Chen Yuanyuan, Sub-Prefects Zou Hanxun and Hu Ziyong, Assistant Magistrates Xing Fu and Ai Yanhui, Vice General Song An, and Staff Generals Ma Liang and Dai Wenyuan died as martyrs at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commissioner Liu Yuzhen, Chizhou Prefect Chen Yuanyuan, Sub-Prefects Zou Hanxun and Hu Ziyong, Assistant Magistrates Xing Fu and Ai Yanhui, Vice General Song An, and Staff Generals Ma Liang and Dai Wenyuan perished with him.

sentences.zh: 胡元煒竟降賊。

translations.literal: Hu Yuanwei in the end surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuanwei ultimately surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 忠濬募人求其屍。

translations.literal: Zhong Jun recruited men to seek his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jun hired men to search for his body.

sentences.zh: 後八日，部卒周昌跡得之，負出，面如生。

translations.literal: Eight days later the soldier Zhou Chang traced and found it, carried it out, and the face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later a soldier named Zhou Chang found it and carried it out; his face looked as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗震悼，贈總督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，入祀昭忠祠，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Wenzong Emperor was shaken with grief, posthumously granted him governor-general rank, bestowed the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, entered his spirit tablet in the Shrine of Loyalty and Fidelity, and gave the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong was stricken with grief. Zhongyuan was posthumously made governor-general, granted hereditary ranks as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Fidelity, and given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal Martyr).

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南平，追念前功，予三等輕車都尉世職，湖南、江西並建專祠，湖北省城與羅澤南合祀三忠祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, when Jiangnan was pacified, his former merit was recalled in memory; he was granted the hereditary office of Third-Rank Light Chariot Commandant, separate shrines were built in Hunan and Jiangxi, and in the Hubei provincial capital he was jointly enshrined with Luo Zenan in the Shrine of the Three Loyal Ones.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, after Jiangnan was pacified, his earlier service was remembered. He was granted the hereditary rank of Third-Rank Light Chariot Commandant. Separate shrines were built in Hunan and Jiangxi, and in the Hubei capital he was enshrined with Luo Zenan in the Shrine of the Three Loyal Ones.

sentences.zh: 忠源歿逾年，湖南有寇警，弟忠淑奉檄募勇助剿。

translations.literal: More than a year after Zhongyuan's death there was a bandit alarm in Hunan; his younger brother Zhong Shu received a dispatch to recruit braves and assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year after Zhongyuan's death, bandits threatened Hunan. His brother Zhong Shu was ordered to raise militia and help suppress them.

sentences.zh: 母陳出私財助餉，並懸重賞以勵眾。

translations.literal: His mother, née Chen, contributed private wealth to aid provisions and also posted heavy rewards to encourage the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Chen, contributed her private wealth to the war fund and offered rich rewards to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 事定，巡撫駱秉章以聞，特旨予忠源父母三代一品封典。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Governor Luo Bingzhang reported it; a special edict granted Zhongyuan's parents the first-rank enfeoffment patent for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, Governor Luo Bingzhang reported the family's service. A special edict granted Zhongyuan's parents the first-rank patent of nobility for three generations.

sentences.zh: 忠源弟三人，忠濬、忠濟、忠淑，族弟忠義、忠信，皆自忠源初起即從軍中。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan had three younger brothers—Zhong Jun, Zhong Ji, and Zhong Shu—and clansman younger brothers Zhong Yi and Zhong Xin; all had followed him in the army from his first rise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan had three younger brothers—Zhong Jun, Zhong Ji, and Zhong Shu—and clansmen Zhong Yi and Zhong Xin. All had followed him into the army from the beginning.

sentences.zh: 忠濬、忠義自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhong Jun and Zhong Yi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jun and Zhong Yi have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 忠濟，從守長沙，城壞，堵缺口，殺登城賊數十，以勇名。

translations.literal: Zhong Ji followed in the defense of Changsha; when the wall was breached he blocked the gap and killed several tens of rebels who climbed the wall, winning fame for courage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ji helped defend Changsha. When the wall was breached he plugged the gap and killed dozens of rebels who had scaled it, earning a reputation for valor.

sentences.zh: 三年，忠源赴湖北，以舊部千人付忠濟留長沙。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhongyuan went to Hubei and left a thousand of his old command with Zhong Ji to remain at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhongyuan went to Hubei and left a thousand of his veterans with Zhong Ji to hold Changsha.

sentences.zh: 忠源勦賊通城，兵單不利，忠濟倍道赴援，戰於桂口，斬賊首陳申子於陣，又破何田俊等，焚其巢；

translations.literal: Zhongyuan suppressed rebels at Tongcheng with few troops and unfavorable conditions; Zhong Ji hurried by double marches to the rescue, fought at Guikou, beheaded the rebel chieftain Chen Shenzi in the battle line, again defeated He Tianjun and others, and burned their nest;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyuan's campaign at Tongcheng went badly with too few men, Zhong Ji force-marched to the rescue. At Guikou he killed the rebel leader Chen Shenzi in battle, routed He Tianjun and others, and burned their stronghold;

sentences.zh: 及援南昌，兩塞城缺，斬賊之先登者。

translations.literal: when he came to relieve Nanchang he twice blocked breaches in the wall and beheaded rebels who first climbed up.
translations.idiomatic: and when he relieved Nanchang he twice sealed breaches in the wall and killed the rebels who broke through first.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張芾疏稱其精敏勇敢，軍中畏服，累功擢候選知府。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Fu memorialized that he was keen, nimble, and brave, feared and respected in the army, and for accumulated merit was promoted to candidate prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Fu memorialized that he was sharp, brave, and respected throughout the army. His accumulated merit won him promotion to candidate prefect.

sentences.zh: 江西解嚴後，忠濟回籍侍母。

translations.literal: After Jiangxi was relieved from martial law, Zhong Ji returned to his native place to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangxi was secured, Zhong Ji went home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 忠源既歿，有旨仍用忠濟及忠濬率兵勦賊。

translations.literal: After Zhongyuan had died, an edict still employed Zhong Ji and Zhong Jun to lead troops in suppressing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyuan's death, an edict ordered Zhong Ji and Zhong Jun to continue leading troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 忠濬方赴援廬州，從和春攻剿。

translations.literal: Zhong Jun was then going to relieve Luzhou and followed Hechun in attack and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jun was marching to relieve Luzhou and fought under Hechun.

sentences.zh: 忠濟為駱秉章調赴藍山、寧遠剿土匪，連破賊解圍，擢道員。

translations.literal: Zhong Ji was transferred by Luo Bingzhang to Lanshan and Ningyuan to suppress local bandits, repeatedly defeated rebels and lifted sieges, and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang sent Zhong Ji to Lanshan and Ningyuan against local bandits. He won repeated victories, lifted sieges, and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 五年，駐防岳州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was stationed on garrison duty at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was posted to garrison Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼攻武昌未下，賊勾結崇陽、通城土匪，忠濟遣兵复通城，遂留駐。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi attacked Wuchang but had not taken it; the rebels colluded with bandits of Chongyang and Tongcheng; Zhong Ji dispatched troops to recover Tongcheng and thereupon remained stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: While Hu Linyi besieged Wuchang without success, rebels allied with bandits in Chongyang and Tongcheng. Zhong Ji sent troops to retake Tongcheng and remained garrisoned there.

sentences.zh: 六年春，江西賊由義寧竄至，忠濟進擊，連破賊壘，而悍黨集數萬，為所圍，力戰三日，營陷，死之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, Jiangxi rebels who had fled from Yining arrived; Zhong Ji advanced to attack, successively breaking rebel stockades, but fierce bandits gathered in tens of thousands; he was surrounded, fought with all his strength for three days; his camp fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, rebels from Jiangxi fled in from Yining. Zhong Ji attacked and broke several stockades, but fierce bands numbering tens of thousands surrounded him. He fought for three days until his camp was overrun and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈按察使銜，予騎都尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of surveillance commissioner, awarded the hereditary office of cavalry commandant, and given the posthumous title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the rank of surveillance commissioner, granted a hereditary cavalry commandant's post, and honored with the posthumous name Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 忠信，少跅弛不羈，年十六，從忠源赴廣西軍。

translations.literal: Zhong Xin in youth was unrestrained and undisciplined; at age sixteen he followed Zhongyuan to the Guangxi army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xin was wild and undisciplined in his youth. At sixteen he followed Zhongyuan to the Guangxi front.

sentences.zh: 犯軍令，忠源將斬之，眾為乞免。

translations.literal: He violated military regulations; Zhongyuan was about to execute him, but the assembly begged for his pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He broke military discipline, and Zhongyuan was about to have him executed until the men pleaded for his life.

sentences.zh: 及遇賊，驍捷敢戰，常為軍鋒，累加擢千總。

translations.literal: When he encountered rebels he was fierce, swift, and daring in battle, frequently serving as the army's vanguard, and was repeatedly promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he proved fierce and fearless, often leading the vanguard, and rose steadily to the rank of company commander.

sentences.zh: 聞忠源被圍廬州，從忠濬赴援。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhongyuan was besieged at Luzhou, he followed Zhong Jun to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Zhongyuan was besieged at Luzhou, he marched with Zhong Jun to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 比至，壁西門外五里墩不得進。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, they were blocked at Wulidun outside the western gate and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, rebel forces blocked them at Wulidun, five li outside the western gate, and they could not get through.

sentences.zh: 忠信夜率壯士十餘人，潛越賊營，縋入城，告以援至。

translations.literal: Zhong Xin at night led more than ten brave men, secretly crossed the rebel camp, was lowered by rope into the city, and reported that relief had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhong Xin led a dozen picked men through the rebel lines, slipped into the city by rope, and brought word that relief was coming.

sentences.zh: 留城中，屢完城缺，縋出攻賊壘，殺賊，擢守備，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He remained in the city, repeatedly repaired breaches in the walls, was lowered out by rope to attack rebel stockades and kill rebels; he was promoted to garrison commandant and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed inside the walls, repeatedly repairing breaches, and slipped out by rope to raid rebel stockades. For these feats he was promoted to garrison commandant and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，忠源揮之去。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhongyuan waved him away to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhongyuan ordered him to escape.

sentences.zh: 五年，從忠濬复廬州，功多，擢游擊，賜號毅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zhong Jun to recover Luzhou; his merits were many; he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Yiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he helped Zhong Jun retake Luzhou. For his distinguished service he was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Yiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 忠濬假歸，代統其眾。

translations.literal: When Zhong Jun took leave to return home, he took command of his troops in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Jun went home on leave, he assumed command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 六年，從和春克三河、巢縣，累擢副將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Hechun in capturing Sanhe and Chaoxian, and was repeatedly promoted to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served under Hechun in the capture of Sanhe and Chaoxian and rose to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 從秦定三規桐城，建議出奇兵夾擊，連破賊營十有六，進逼城下，賊大出，迎擊，進至東門外，躍馬越壕擒賊將，砲丸中左腋，殞於陣。

translations.literal: Following Qin Dingsan in planning against Tongcheng, he proposed sending surprise forces in a pincer attack, successively breaking sixteen rebel camps and pressing close to the walls; the rebels came out in force and he met them in battle; advancing to outside the eastern gate, he leaped his horse over the moat and captured a rebel general; a cannonball struck his left armpit and he died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Qin Dingsan in the campaign against Tongcheng, he proposed a flanking maneuver with surprise troops, stormed sixteen rebel camps, and pushed to the foot of the walls. When the rebels poured out to meet him, he rode to the eastern gate, leaped the moat, and seized a rebel general before a cannonball struck his left side and killed him in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 予雲騎尉世職，諡忠節。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary office of cloud cavalry commandant and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hereditary cloud cavalry commandant's post and honored with the posthumous name Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 忠濟、忠信並附祀忠源專祠。

translations.literal: Zhong Ji and Zhong Xin were both enshrined alongside Zhongyuan in his dedicated temple.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhong Ji and Zhong Xin were granted secondary enshrinement in Zhongyuan's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南，字仲岳，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Luo Zenan, style name Zhongyue, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zenan, styled Zhongyue, was from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生，講學鄉里，從遊甚眾。

translations.literal: A provincial licentiate, he lectured in his home district and had very many followers.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he taught in his home district and drew a large circle of students.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he was recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was nominated as a filial and upright candidate.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪犯長沙，澤南在籍倡辦團練。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Cantonese rebels attacked Changsha, Zenan while at home initiated the organization of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the Guangdong rebels threatened Changsha, Zenan organized local militia while still at home.

sentences.zh: 三年，以勞敘訓導。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of his labors he was registered for the post of assistant prefect of education.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his service was rewarded with registration for a post as assistant prefect of education.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓奉命督鄉兵，檄剿平桂東土匪，擢知縣。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan on imperial order supervised the district militia and dispatched him to suppress and pacify bandits in Guidong; he was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan was ordered to command the district militia, he dispatched Zenan to suppress bandits in Guidong, and Zenan was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 江忠源援江西，乞師於國籓，乃令澤南率以往。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan went to aid Jiangxi and begged troops from Guofan; Guofan thereupon ordered Zenan to lead them thither.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Zhongyuan marched to relieve Jiangxi, he asked Guofan for reinforcements, and Guofan sent Zenan to lead them there.

sentences.zh: 所部多起書生，初臨行陣，戰南昌城下，爭奮搏，死者數人。

translations.literal: His command consisted largely of scholars; on first facing the battle line, they fought below the walls of Nanchang, each vying to plunge into combat; several died.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were mostly scholars. In their first taste of battle under the walls of Nanchang, they fought with such eagerness that several were killed.

sentences.zh: 國籓聞之，喜曰：「湘軍果可用。」

translations.literal: Guofan heard of it and said with delight: "The Hunan Army is indeed fit for use."
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan heard of it, he rejoiced and said, "The Hunan Army is truly worth deploying."

sentences.zh: 及圍解，剿安福土匪，以三百人破賊數千，擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he suppressed bandits in Anfu; with three hundred men he broke rebels numbering thousands and was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted, he suppressed bandits in Anfu, routing thousands of rebels with only three hundred men, and was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歸湖南，剿平永興土匪，所部增至千人，屯衡州。

translations.literal: Returning to Hunan, he suppressed and pacified bandits in Yongxing; his command increased to a thousand men, and he encamped at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Hunan, he pacified bandits in Yongxing, expanded his force to a thousand men, and encamped at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 與國籓簡軍實，更營制，教練歷半載。

translations.literal: Together with Guofan he inspected the army's strength, reformed the military organization, and trained for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He and Guofan reviewed troop strength, reorganized the regimental system, and drilled for six months.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，偕塔齊布進攻岳州，以大橋為賊所必爭，堅扼不動，伺便突出擊之，三戰皆捷，殲賊千。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, together with Taqibu he advanced to attack Yuezhou; since Big Bridge was a place the rebels were certain to contest, he held it firmly without moving, waited for an opportunity to sally out and strike, won all three encounters, and destroyed a thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year he joined Taqibu in the assault on Yuezhou. Holding Big Bridge—a choke point the rebels had to fight for—he refused to budge until the moment was right, then struck. Three battles, three victories, and a thousand rebels destroyed.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，破高橋賊壘九，賊退踞城陵磯，偕塔齊布乘勝進擊，連破賊營，賊遂遁走，擢知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month he broke nine rebel stockades at Gaoqiao; the rebels withdrew to hold Chenglingji; together with Taqibu he pressed the victory in pursuit, successively breaking rebel camps, and the rebels then fled; he was promoted to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month he stormed nine stockades at Gaoqiao. The rebels fell back to Chenglingji, where he and Taqibu pressed the attack, broke camp after camp, and drove them into full retreat. He was promoted to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 自是湘軍名始播，以澤南與塔齊布並稱。

translations.literal: From this time the name of the Hunan Army first spread abroad, and Zenan and Taqibu were mentioned together.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Hunan Army's reputation spread, and Zenan and Taqibu were spoken of in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 轉戰而東，复崇陽，擊走咸寧賊，再敗之金牛，進駐紫坊。

translations.literal: Turning to fight eastward, he recovered Chongyang, drove off the rebels at Xianning, defeated them again at Jinniu, and advanced to encamp at Zifang.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting eastward, he retook Chongyang, drove the Xianning rebels back, defeated them again at Jinniu, and established camp at Zifang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓會諸將於金口，議攻武昌。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan assembled the generals at Jinkou and deliberated on attacking Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan gathered his generals at Jinkou to plan the assault on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 澤南繪圖獻方略，謂由紫坊出武昌有二道，請以塔齊布扼洪山，而自攻花園。
