translations.literal: Zenan drew a map and presented a plan of strategy, saying that from Zifang there were two routes toward Wuchang; he asked that Taqibu hold Hongshan while he himself attacked Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan submitted a map and battle plan, noting two routes from Zifang toward Wuchang. He proposed that Taqibu block Hongshan while he assaulted Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 賊萬餘踞花園，築堅壘，一枕大江，一瀕青林湖，一跨長堤，深溝重柵，峙江東岸，與蝦蟆磯對壘。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand rebels held Huayuan and built solid stockades: one resting against the great river, one bordering Qinglin Lake, one spanning the long dike; with deep moats and heavy palisades they stood on the eastern bank of the river, facing Xiama Ji in opposing camps.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand rebels held Huayuan behind three fortified positions—one on the great river, one on Qinglin Lake, one astride the long dike—deep moats and heavy palisades lining the east bank opposite Xiama Ji.

sentences.zh: 列巨砲向江內外，分阻水陸兩路。

translations.literal: They lined heavy cannon toward the river inside and outside, dividing to block both the water and land routes.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy guns lined the inner and outer riverbanks, blocking both land and water approaches.

sentences.zh: 澤南率隊直趨花園，賊憑木城發砲。

translations.literal: Zenan led his brigade straight toward Huayuan; the rebels relied on their wooden walls to fire cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan led his brigade straight at Huayuan, and the rebels answered with cannon fire from behind their wooden walls.

sentences.zh: 士卒蛇行而進，三伏三起，已逼賊壘，分兵奪賊舟，舟賊退，營賊亦亂，三壘同下。

translations.literal: The soldiers advanced in snake-like crawling; thrice they lay flat and thrice they rose; already they pressed close to the rebel stockades; dividing forces they seized rebel boats; the rebels on the boats withdrew, the rebels in the camps also fell into disorder, and all three stockades fell together.
translations.idiomatic: His men crawled forward in low skirmish lines, dropping and rising three times before reaching the stockades. Detachments seized the rebel boats; as the boat crews fled, the garrisons broke, and all three positions fell at once.

sentences.zh: 翌日又破鮎魚套賊營，其竄洪山者，為塔齊布所扼，賊夜棄城走。

translations.literal: The next day he again broke the rebel camp at Miaoyutao; those who fled toward Hongshan were blocked by Taqibu; the rebels abandoned the city at night and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he stormed Miaoyutao. Rebels who tried to escape toward Hongshan were blocked by Taqibu, and that night they abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽皆复，距會議僅七日。

translations.literal: Wuchang and Hanyang were both recovered, only seven days from the conference.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang and Hanyang were both retaken—just seven days after the council of war.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，以道員記名，尋授浙江寧紹台道，國籓請仍留軍。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, he was registered by name as a circuit intendant; soon afterward he was appointed to the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit in Zhejiang; Guofan requested that he remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the victory reached the court, and he was placed on the list for circuit intendant. He was soon appointed to the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit in Zhejiang, but Guofan asked that he stay with the army.

sentences.zh: 賊據興國，分陷大冶。

translations.literal: The rebels held Xingguo and in detachments took Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Xingguo and had seized Daye in a secondary thrust.

sentences.zh: 澤南馳克興國，塔齊布亦克武昌、大冶，乃規取田家鎮。

translations.literal: Zenan swiftly captured Xingguo; Taqibu also captured Wuchang and Daye; thereupon they planned to take Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan swiftly retook Xingguo while Taqibu secured Daye from the Wuchang front; they then turned their sights on Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 賊以鐵鎖截水師，而踞半壁山為犄角，夾江而守。

translations.literal: The rebels used iron chains to block the navy and held Banbishan as a corner position, guarding on both sides of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blocked the river with iron chains and held Banbishan as a flank position, defending both banks.

sentences.zh: 澤南進駐馬嶺坳，距半壁山三里許。

translations.literal: Zenan advanced to encamp at Maling'ao, about three li from Banbishan.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan advanced and encamped at Maling'ao, roughly three li from Banbishan.

sentences.zh: 賊數千突來犯，而由田鎮渡江來援者近萬人。

translations.literal: Several thousand rebels suddenly came to attack, while those crossing the river from Tianjiazhen to reinforce numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand rebels attacked suddenly, and nearly ten thousand more were crossing the river from Tianjiazhen to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 澤南兵僅二千，令堅伏，度賊懈，奮擊，賊大潰，後路為我軍所阻，墜崖死者數千，遂奪半壁山，水師斷橫江鐵鎖，燔賊舟，克田家鎮，賜號普鏗額巴圖魯，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: Zenan's force numbered only two thousand; he ordered them to lie concealed; estimating that the rebels had slackened, he struck with vigor; the rebels broke in great rout; their rear route was blocked by our army; several thousand fell from cliffs and died; he then seized Banbishan; the navy cut the iron chains spanning the river, burned rebel boats, and captured Tianjiazhen; he was granted the title Pukeng'e Batulu and given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With only two thousand men, Zenan kept his troops hidden until the rebels relaxed their guard, then struck. They broke and fled, but their retreat was cut off and thousands plunged to their deaths from the cliffs. He took Banbishan; the navy severed the river chains and burned the rebel fleet; Tianjiazhen fell. He was granted the title Pukeng'e Baturu and promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時議水陸軍分三路進剿，總督楊霈督江北岸軍，澤南偕塔齊布攻其南，曾國籓督水師循江下。

translations.literal: At this time it was proposed that the land and river forces advance in three routes for suppression; Governor-general Yang Yining supervised the army on the north bank of the river; Zenan together with Taqibu attacked to the south; Zeng Guofan supervised the navy in descent down the river.
translations.idiomatic: A three-pronged land-and-river campaign was then approved. Governor-general Yang Yining commanded the north-bank forces; Zenan and Taqibu struck from the south; Guofan led the fleet downstream.

sentences.zh: 霈不能軍，賊复北趨，乃偕塔齊布改北渡江，复廣濟、黃梅。

translations.literal: Yining could not maintain his army; the rebels again pressed northward; thereupon together with Taqibu he changed course, crossed the river northward, and recovered Guangji and Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang proved unable to hold his command. When the rebels again thrust north, Zenan joined Taqibu in crossing the river to the north bank and retaking Guangji and Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 賊退踞孔隴驛、小池口，澤南約諸軍會攻。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew and occupied Konglong Post Station and Xiaochikou; Zinan arranged for the various armies to join in attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back and held Konglong Station and Xiaochikou; Zinan coordinated the allied forces for a joint assault.

sentences.zh: 渡江未半，賊來犯，軍少卻，澤南傷臂，仍指揮衝突，分兵破街口賊壘，賊酋羅大綱引去。

translations.literal: Having crossed not yet half the river, the rebels came to attack; the army slightly retreated. Zinan wounded his arm, yet still directed the charge, divided troops to break the rebel fort at Jiekou, and the rebel chieftain Luo Dagang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-crossing, the rebels struck and the force briefly gave ground. Zinan, though wounded in the arm, continued to direct the assault, sent detachments to smash the rebel stronghold at Jiekou, and drove off the rebel leader Luo Dagang.

sentences.zh: 是役也，五千人破賊二萬，賊乃盡撤沿江諸營，並守九江。

translations.literal: In this battle, five thousand men defeated twenty thousand rebels; the rebels then entirely withdrew all camps along the river and concentrated on defending Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In that engagement, five thousand men routed twenty thousand rebels. The rebels thereupon abandoned their riverside camps and massed their defenses at Jiujiang alone.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布圍攻之，澤南別剿盔山，遏湖口援賊。

translations.literal: Taqibu besieged and attacked it; Zinan separately suppressed Kuishan, blocking Hukou relief rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Taqibu laid siege to Jiujiang while Zinan mounted a separate operation against Kuishan to cut off rebel reinforcements from Hukou.

sentences.zh: 會水師入鄱陽湖，為賊所襲，輜重皆失。

translations.literal: It happened that the water force entered Poyang Lake and was attacked by rebels; all baggage and supplies were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the naval force entered Poyang Lake and was ambushed by the rebels, losing all its supplies and baggage.

sentences.zh: 國籓馳入澤南營，而水師阻湖口不得出。

translations.literal: Guofan rode hastily into Zinan's camp, while the water force was blocked at Hukou and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan hurried to Zinan's camp, but the fleet was trapped at Hukou and could not break free.

sentences.zh: 五年，湖北官軍屢敗，武昌复陷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Hubei government troops repeatedly suffered defeats, and Wuchang fell again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign, the imperial armies in Hubei suffered repeated defeats and Wuchang fell once more.

sentences.zh: 澤南從國籓入南昌，赴援饒州，戰於陳家山、大松林，大破賊，复弋陽。

translations.literal: Zinan followed Guofan into Nanchang, went to relieve Raozhou, fought at Chenjiashan and Dasonglin, greatly defeated the rebels, and recovered Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zinan accompanied Guofan to Nanchang and marched to relieve Raozhou. At Chenjiashan and Dasonglin he inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebels and recovered Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 又援廣信，破賊於城西烏石山，復之。

translations.literal: He again relieved Guangxin, defeated the rebels at Wushi Mountain west of the city, and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched to the relief of Guangxin, routed the rebels at Wushi Mountain west of the city, and retook it.

sentences.zh: 連復興安、德興、浮梁，進剿義寧。

translations.literal: He successively recovered Xing'an, Dexing, and Fuliang, and advanced to suppress Yining.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to recover Xing'an, Dexing, and Fuliang in succession, then pressed the campaign into Yining.

sentences.zh: 敗賊於梁口、鼇嶺，复義寧，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Liangkou and Aoling, recovered Yining, and was given the rank title of Bureau Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After victories at Liangkou and Aoling he retook Yining and was granted the honorary rank of Bureau Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 澤南見江西軍事不得要領，上書國籓，略曰：「九江逼近江寧，兼牽制武昌，故賊以全力爭之。

translations.literal: Zinan saw that Jiangxi military affairs lacked grasp of essentials; he wrote to Guofan, briefly saying: "Jiujiang is close to Jiangning and also restrains Wuchang; therefore the rebels contend for it with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Jiangxi campaign lacked a coherent strategy, Zinan wrote to Guofan in summary: "Jiujiang lies near Jiangning and also pins down Wuchang, which is why the rebels are contesting it with their full strength.

sentences.zh: 犯弋陽，援廣信，從信水下彭蠡，抄我師之右；

translations.literal: They violate Yiyang, relieve Guangxin, descend from the Xin River into Poyang Lake, and outflank the right of our army;
translations.idiomatic: They strike at Yiyang, reinforce Guangxin, come down the Xin River into Lake Poyang, and threaten our right flank;

sentences.zh: 據義寧，守梅嶺，從修水下彭蠡，抄我師之左。

translations.literal: They hold Yining, guard Meiling Pass, descend from the Xiu River into Poyang Lake, and outflank the left of our army.
translations.idiomatic: they hold Yining, garrison Meiling Pass, descend the Xiu River into Lake Poyang, and threaten our left flank.

sentences.zh: 今兩處平定，九江門戶漸固，惟湖北通城等處群盜如毛。

translations.literal: Now both places are pacified and Jiujiang's gateway is gradually secure, but in places such as Tongcheng in Hubei, bandits are as numerous as hairs.
translations.idiomatic: With both routes now secured, Jiujiang's approaches are growing firm—but in Tongcheng and other parts of Hubei, rebel bands swarm like weeds.

sentences.zh: 江西之義寧、武寧，湖南之平江、巴陵，終無安枕之日。

translations.literal: Yining and Wuning in Jiangxi, and Pingjiang and Baling in Hunan will ultimately have no day of peaceful sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Yining and Wuning in Jiangxi, Pingjiang and Baling in Hunan—these counties will never know a day of peace so long as those bands remain.

sentences.zh: 欲制九江之命，宜從武昌而下；

translations.literal: To control Jiujiang's fate, one should proceed from Wuchang downward;
translations.idiomatic: To seize the fate of Jiujiang, one must strike south from Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 如解武昌之圍，宜從崇、通而入。

translations.literal: If one wishes to relieve the siege of Wuchang, one should enter from Chongyang and Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: and to lift the siege of Wuchang, one should advance through Chongyang and Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，當以湖口水師、九江陸師截賊船之上下，更選勁旅掃崇、通以進武昌，由武昌以規九江。

translations.literal: For the present plan, the Hukou water force and Jiujiang land force should intercept rebel ships going up and down; further select crack troops to sweep Chongyang and Tongcheng to advance on Wuchang, and from Wuchang plan for Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The present plan should be this: use the Hukou fleet and Jiujiang land forces to block rebel shipping up and down the river, then send a picked column to sweep Chongyang and Tongcheng and drive on Wuchang—from Wuchang to take aim at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 東南全局，庶有轉機。」

translations.literal: For the overall southeastern situation, there may then be a turning point."
translations.idiomatic: Only thus may the whole southeastern front find its turning point.

sentences.zh: 國籓據以上聞，遂命澤南移師湖北會剿，以塔齊布舊將彭三元、普承堯所部寶勇隸之，凡五千人。

translations.literal: Guofan reported the above to the throne and thereupon ordered Zinan to transfer his army to Hubei for joint suppression, attaching to him the Baoyong troops under Taqibu's former generals Peng Sanyuan and Pu Chengyao—altogether five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan forwarded this memorial to the throne and ordered Zinan to shift his forces to Hubei for a joint campaign. Peng Sanyuan and Pu Chengyao, former subordinates of Taqibu, were placed under his command with their Baoyong regiment—five thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 九月，至通城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he arrived at Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 賊號數萬，皆烏合，一戰而潰。

translations.literal: The rebels numbered tens of thousands in claim, but all were a motley crowd; after one battle they collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels claimed numbers in the tens of thousands, but they were a rabble—one battle and they scattered.

sentences.zh: 進奪桂口要隘，克崇陽，駐軍羊樓峒。

translations.literal: Advancing, he seized the strategic pass of Guikou, captured Chongyang, and encamped at Yangloudong.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward, took the strategic pass at Guikou, captured Chongyang, and encamped at Yangloudong.

sentences.zh: 悍賊韋俊、石達開合黨二萬餘自蒲圻來犯，截擊走之。

translations.literal: Fierce rebels Wei Jun and Shi Dakai combined their factions—more than twenty thousand—from Puchi to come attack; he intercepted, struck, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The formidable rebels Wei Jun and Shi Dakai joined forces—more than twenty thousand strong—and marched from Puchi to attack. Zinan intercepted them and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼來勞師，合攻蒲圻，復其城，乘霧進克咸寧。

translations.literal: Hu Linji came to encourage the troops; together they attacked Puchi, recovered its city, and taking advantage of fog advanced to capture Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linji arrived to review the troops. Together they assaulted Puchi, retook the city, and exploiting a fog advanced to capture Xianning.

sentences.zh: 自是武昌以南無賊踪。

translations.literal: From this, south of Wuchang there were no traces of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: From that point south of Wuchang, rebel activity ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 十一月，師抵紫坊，與林翼議進取次第。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the army reached Zifang and discussed with Linji the order of advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the army reached Zifang, where Zinan and Linji plotted the sequence of their advance.

sentences.zh: 澤南屯洪山，林翼屯城南堤上，水師駐金口。

translations.literal: Zinan encamped at Hongshan, Linji encamped on the dike south of the city, and the water force was stationed at Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zinan camped at Mount Hong, Linji on the southern embankment outside the city walls, and the fleet anchored at Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 賊於城外築堅壘十三，與城埒。

translations.literal: The rebels built thirteen solid forts outside the city, equal to the city in strength.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls the rebels had raised thirteen fortified camps, each as strong as the city itself.

sentences.zh: 初戰，賊二萬出十字街，林翼與交綏，數卻數進。

translations.literal: In the first battle, twenty thousand rebels came out from Shizi Street; Linji engaged them, repeatedly retreating and repeatedly advancing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first engagement twenty thousand rebels poured out through Shizi Street. Linji locked with them in a seesaw fight, falling back and surging forward by turns.

sentences.zh: 澤南與李續賓分兩路潛抄賊壘，破十字街營，盡毀城東南諸壘。

translations.literal: Zinan and Li Xubing divided into two routes to secretly outflank the rebel forts, broke the Shizi Street camp, and utterly destroyed all forts southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zinan and Li Xubing split into two columns, stole around the rebel positions, smashed the Shizi Street camp, and tore down every fort southeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 八步街口為我軍通江要路，塘角為賊糧運所出，先後攻破之，焚其船廠，環西北賊壘亦盡。

translations.literal: Babujiekou was our army's vital route to the river; Tangjiao was where rebel grain transport issued forth—they were successively broken through, their shipyard was burned, and the rebel forts encircling the northwest were also all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Babujiekou was the army's vital corridor to the river; Tangjiao the rebels' grain supply line. Both were taken in turn, the shipyard burned, and the northwestern ring of rebel camps wiped out.

sentences.zh: 賊又由望山門外葺石壘二，揮軍蹋平之；

translations.literal: The rebels also repaired two stone forts outside Wangshan Gate; he commanded the troops to trample them flat;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rebuilt two stone fortifications outside Wangshan Gate; he ordered his men forward and leveled them;

sentences.zh: 又迭於窯灣、塘角逐賊，殲戮數千，賊遂閉城不出。

translations.literal: Again and again he fought the rebels at Yaowan and Tangjiao, slaying several thousand; the rebels then closed the city and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: then fought them again and again at Yaowan and Tangjiao, killing several thousand. The rebels finally shut the gates and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 石達開自崇陽敗後，竄入江西，勢复張。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai, after his defeat at Chongyang, fled into Jiangxi, and his power revived and expanded.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Chongyang, Shi Dakai fled into Jiangxi and gathered strength once more.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓檄澤南迴援，澤南以武漢為南北樞紐，若湘勇驟撤，胡林翼一軍不能獨立，現在賊糧將盡，功在垂成，舍之非計。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan issued an order for Zinan to return and reinforce; Zinan held that Wuhan was the pivot between north and south—if the Hunan Braves were suddenly withdrawn, Hu Linji's single army could not stand alone; presently the rebels' grain was nearly exhausted and success was near at hand—abandoning it would not be a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan ordered Zinan back to Jiangxi, but Zinan argued that Wuhan was the hinge of north and south: if the Hunan troops were suddenly pulled away, Hu Linji's force could not hold alone. The rebels' supplies were nearly spent and victory was within reach—to abandon the siege now would be folly.

sentences.zh: 其父年八十，貽書軍中勗以忠義，林翼以聞，六年二月，詔特予澤南祖父母、父母二品封典，以示旌異。

translations.literal: His father, eighty years old, sent a letter to the army encouraging loyalty and righteousness; Linji reported this. In the second month of the sixth year, an edict specially conferred on Zinan's grandparents and parents second-rank posthumous honors, to show special recognition.
translations.idiomatic: His father, eighty years old, wrote to the camp exhorting him to loyalty and duty; Linji forwarded the letter to the throne. In the second month of the sixth year, an edict specially granted second-rank posthumous honors to Zinan's grandparents and parents in token of distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊開門出撲，澤南親督戰。

translations.literal: In the third month, the rebels opened the gates and came out to assault; Zinan personally supervised the battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels threw open the gates and rushed out to attack; Zinan personally directed the fighting.

sentences.zh: 援賊大隊繼至，我軍自洪山馳下，奮擊追逐，直抵城下，飛砲中澤南左額，血流被面。

translations.literal: Large rebel relief columns arrived in succession; our army galloped down from Hongshan, fought fiercely in pursuit, and pressed straight to the city walls—a flying cannonball struck Zinan on the left forehead, blood flowing over his face.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements arrived in force. Our troops charged down from Mount Hong, struck hard in pursuit, and pressed to the walls—when a cannon shot caught Zinan on the left brow, blood streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 駐馬一時許，歸洪山，猶危坐營外，指畫戰狀。

translations.literal: He halted his horse for about an hour, returned to Hongshan, and still sat upright outside the camp, directing the battle situation.
translations.idiomatic: He reined in for the better part of an hour, then rode back to Mount Hong and, still bleeding, sat upright outside his tent, sketching out the disposition of the battle.

sentences.zh: 翌日，卒於軍。

translations.literal: The next day, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 文宗震悼，詔依巡撫例議卹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was deeply shocked and grieved; an edict ordered mourning compensation to be deliberated according to the precedent for governors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was stricken with grief and ordered posthumous honors befitting a provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 賜其父嘉旦頭品頂戴，子兆作、兆升皆舉人，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: His father Jiadan was granted a first-rank finial; sons Zhaozuo and Zhaosheng were both provincial graduates; a hereditary Captaincy was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiadan was granted a first-rank official's finial; his sons Zhaozuo and Zhaosheng, both provincial graduates, were given the hereditary rank of Captain of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 入祀昭忠祠，本籍、湖北、江西建立專祠，諡忠節。

translations.literal: He was entered into worship at the Shrine of Loyalty and Martyrdom; dedicated shrines were established in his native place, Hubei, and Jiangxi; his posthumous title was Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal and Faithful Officials, with dedicated temples raised in his home province, Hubei, and Jiangxi. His posthumous title was Loyal Integrity.

sentences.zh: 及江南平，穆宗追念前勞，加一雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, Emperor Muzong recalled his earlier labors and added one hereditary Cloud-Cavalry Captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan region was finally pacified, Emperor Muzong, recalling his earlier service, added a hereditary Cloud-Cavalry Captaincy to the family's honors.

sentences.zh: 澤南所著有《小學韻語》、《西銘講義》、《周易附說》、《人極衍義》、《姚江學辨》、《方輿要覽》諸書。

translations.literal: Works composed by Zinan include Elementary Learning in Rhyme, Lectures on the Western Inscription, Supplementary Notes on the Book of Changes, Extended Meaning of the Human Ultimate, Discernment of the Yaojiang School, and Essentials of Geography, among other books.
translations.idiomatic: Zinan's writings included Elementary Learning in Rhyme, Lectures on the Western Inscription, Supplementary Notes on the Book of Changes, Extended Meaning of the Human Ultimate, Discernment of the Yaojiang School, Essentials of Geography, and others.

sentences.zh: 體用兼備，一宗程、朱，學者稱羅山先生。

translations.literal: Substance and function both complete, he took as his single school Cheng and Zhu; scholars called him Master Luoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Equal in cultivation and practical application, he devoted himself wholly to the Cheng-Zhu school of Neo-Confucianism. Scholars honored him as Master Luoshan.

sentences.zh: 嘗論兵略，謂大學首章「知止」數語盡之，《左傳》「再衰」、「三竭」之言，其註腳也。

translations.literal: He once discussed military strategy, saying that the several phrases on "knowing where to stop" in the first chapter of the Great Learning exhaust it; the words on "declining a second time" and "exhausted a third time" in the Zuo Commentary are its annotations.
translations.idiomatic: Discussing military strategy, he said the opening of the Great Learning—those lines on knowing when to stop—contained the whole doctrine, and the Zuo Commentary's warning that spirit flags at the second drum and fails at the third was its practical illustration.

sentences.zh: 弟子從軍多成名將，最著者李續賓、李續宜、王珍、劉騰鴻、蔣益澧，皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Many of his disciples who followed the army became famed generals; the most renowned were Li Xubing, Li Xuyi, Wang Zhen, Liu Tenghong, and Jiang Yili—all have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his disciples who took the field rose to eminence as commanders; the most celebrated—Li Xubing, Li Xuyi, Wang Zhen, Liu Tenghong, and Jiang Yili—each has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 其早死兵事名未顯者，有鍾近衡，少事澤南，以克己自勵，日記言動，有過立起自責。

translations.literal: Among those who died early in military affairs with fame not yet manifest was Zhong Jinheng, who in youth served Zenan, took self-restraint as encouragement, kept a diary of words and deeds, and when at fault would immediately rise to blame himself.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zenan's disciples who died young before their fame spread was Zhong Jinheng. He had studied under Zenan from boyhood, disciplined himself rigorously, kept a diary of his conduct, and rose at once to reproach himself whenever he found fault.

sentences.zh: 澤南語劉蓉曰：「吾門為己之學，鍾生其庶幾乎！」

translations.literal: Zenan said to Liu Rong: "In our school the learning is for the self—perhaps young Zhong comes near to it!"
translations.idiomatic: Zenan told Liu Rong, "Our school teaches self-cultivation for its own sake—young Zhong may come close to living it!"

sentences.zh: 從平郴、桂土匪，敘從九品，

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the bandits of Chen and Gui, and was recorded for promotion to the ninth-rank follower.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify banditry in Chenzhou and Guilin and was entered on the rolls for the ninth-rank follower post.

sentences.zh: 粵匪由江寧上竄犯岳州，偕弟近濂各將五百人從王珍破賊於靖港，追至蒲圻羊樓峒，戰失利，死之。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebels fled upward from Jiangning and attacked Yuezhou; he and his younger brother Jinlian each led five hundred men and followed Wang Zhen in defeating rebels at Jinggang, pursued them to Yanglou Cave in Puqi, fought with unfavorable outcome, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled down from Nanjing and struck at Yuezhou, he and his brother Jinlian each commanded five hundred men under Wang Zhen and routed the enemy at Jinggang. Pursuing them to Yanglou Cave in Puqi, they were defeated in battle and killed.

sentences.zh: 王珍退保岳州，賊又大至，近濂亦戰歿。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen withdrew to defend Yuezhou; the rebels came again in force, and Jinlian also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen fell back to defend Yuezhou, but the rebels returned in strength and Jinlian was killed in battle as well.

sentences.zh: 易良幹、謝邦翰，並戰死南昌城下。

translations.literal: Yi Lianggan and Xie Banghan both died in battle below the walls of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Lianggan and Xie Banghan also died fighting beneath the walls of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 邦翰死後，李續賓代領其眾，所稱「湘右營」者是也。

translations.literal: After Banghan's death, Li Xubin took command of his troops in his stead; this was the force called the "Xiang Right Battalion."
translations.idiomatic: After Banghan's death Li Xubin took over his command—the unit known as the "Xiang Right Battalion."

sentences.zh: 諸人皆湘鄉人，後並附祀澤南專祠。

translations.literal: All these men were natives of Xiangxiang, and afterward were jointly enshrined in Zenan's dedicated shrine.
translations.idiomatic: All were natives of Xiangxiang and were later enshrined together in Zenan's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 論曰：湖南募勇出境勦賊，自江忠源始。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Hunan's raising of braves to cross the border and suppress rebels began with Jiang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The practice of Hunan recruiting militia to campaign beyond the province began with Jiang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓立湘軍，則羅澤南實左右之。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan established the Xiang Army, Luo Zenan was in truth his right-hand support.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan built the Xiang Army, Luo Zenan was his indispensable right hand.

sentences.zh: 樸誠勇敢之風，皆二人所提倡也。

translations.literal: The spirit of plain sincerity and brave courage was promoted by both these men.
translations.idiomatic: The ethos of plainspoken loyalty and fearless courage was theirs to establish.

sentences.zh: 忠源受知於文宗，已大用而遽殞。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan won recognition from the Wenzong Emperor, was already greatly employed, and suddenly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan had won Emperor Wenzong's trust and was on the verge of great power when he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 澤南定力爭上游之策，功未竟而身殲，天下惜之。

translations.literal: Zenan firmly held to the strategy of striving for the upper stream; his merit was not completed when his person was destroyed, and all under heaven mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zenan held fast to the strategy of seizing the upper hand. His work was unfinished when he fell, and the empire mourned him.

sentences.zh: 忠源言兵事一疏，澤南籌援鄂一書，為大局成敗所關，並列之以存龜鑑。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan's one memorial on military affairs and Zenan's one letter planning relief for Hubei bore on the success or failure of the great design; both are set forth together to preserve them as a mirror for future guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan's memorial on military affairs and Zenan's letter on relieving Hubei were both decisive to the larger campaign. They are recorded here together as a lesson for posterity.

sentences.zh: 此大將風規，不第為楚材之弁冕已。

translations.literal: This is the bearing and rule of great generals—not merely the cap and insignia of Chu talent alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is the standard of great commanders—not merely the ornament of Hunan's finest sons.
